parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
State an expression for the electric field strength E at a distance r from a point charge Q in a
vacuum.
State the name of any other symbol used.

markscheme_points.text: where ε0 is permittivity (of free space)

hints: Hint 1: Focus on the physical mechanism in A Level Physics theory and principles that causes this behavior.
Hint 2: Rearrange the algebraic equation to isolate the target variable before substituting numerical values.
parts.proper_answer: (E =) Q / 4πε0r2; where ε0 is permittivity (of free space)
walkthrough:

Step 2: **Substitute Values & Calculate**
Work through the substitution and calculation systematically:

Verify intermediate arithmetic carefully.

Step 3: **Units & Significant Figures**
State the final result clearly with appropriate significant figures (typically 2 or 3 s.f.) and standard SI units.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
An electron is situated at point P.
Without calculation, state and explain the variation in the magnitude of the acceleration of the
electron as it moves from the position where x = 3 cm to the position where x = 7 cm.

markscheme_points.text: force = field strength × charge and force = mass × acceleration or acceleration is proportional to field strength
(from x = 3.0 cm) to x = 5.0 cm: acceleration decreases
at x = 5.0 cm: acceleration is a minimum
from x = 5.0 cm (to x = 7.0 cm): acceleration increases

hints: Hint 1: Focus on the physical mechanism in A Level Physics theory and principles that causes this behavior.
Hint 2: Rearrange the algebraic equation to isolate the target variable before substituting numerical values.
Hint 3: Ensure all quantities are expressed in standard SI base units and verify your intermediate arithmetic before writing the final result to 2 or 3 significant figures.
Hint 4: Clearly show every intermediate algebraic substitution and ensure your final value has correct physical units.
